## Comments and notations {.center-content}
- We define
$$ u(\tau,x) \sim 
   \sum_n \color{red}{{\cal A}_n(x) \;e^{i\omega_{n}\tau} } \quad ,  \quad {\cal A}_n(x) \equiv \langle\alpha_n, u_0\rangle v_n(x),$$ 
and
$${\cal A}_n(\tau,x) \equiv \color{red}{{\cal A}_n(x) \;e^{i\omega_{n}\tau} }. $$

- We call "relative modal weight" the quantity 
$$ W_n^\infty(\tau)=\frac{\left\vert\color{blue}{{\cal A}_n^\infty(\tau)} \right\vert}{\max_n \left\vert\color{blue}{{\cal A}_n^\infty(\tau)} \right\vert}\quad,\quad \color{blue}{{\cal A}_n^\infty(\tau)} \equiv {\cal A}_n(\tau,x)\vert_{x=x_{\mathscr I^+}} $$ 

- It is also insightful to consider the beating between eigenvalues of opposite real part (i.e. $\omega_n$ and $-\bar \omega_n$) with
$$\left\vert\frac{\color{blue}{{\cal A}_n^\infty(\tau)}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert\quad \text{ instead of }\quad \left\vert\color{blue}{{\cal A}_n^\infty(\tau)}\right\vert$$

- We now illustrate the Algebraically Special (AS) 'stagnation' in the 4 cases of study. Some of the axis labels and colorbar titles are incorrect. Please refer to the title of the slide instead.

## Comments [☆]{style="color: red;"}
- We assess $|\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n \tau}|$ with a suitable normalisation. If $\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}$ is not numerically stable, then we are making (good looking) plots that change for each grid resolution.
- We need call "relative modal weight" the quantity 
$$ W_n(\tau)=\frac{\left\vert\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}\right\vert}{\max_n \left\vert\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n\tau}\right\vert},$$ 


In order to take into account the beating between eigenvalues of opposite real part, it is natural to evaluate
$$\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{Re}(\omega_n)\geq 0 \\ \mathrm{Im}(\omega_n)\geq 0}}\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+}e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}$$


We will consider
$$ W_n^{c.c.}(\tau)=\frac{\left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert}{\max_n \left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert},$$ 

$$ W_n^{c.c.,n.r.}(\tau)=\left\vert\frac{\mathcal{A}_n^{{\mathscr I}^+} e^{i\omega_n\tau}+c.c.}{2}\right\vert,$$ 

-->

We have fixed the parameters $a/M=0.01$, $m=0$ and we change $\theta$
